Meta Global AI Developer Hackathon Participant Guide

Welcome to the Meta Global AI Developer Hackathon (the “Hackathon”)! We’re thrilled to have you on board.

This guide is your all-in-one resource for the event, including schedule, rules, technical resources, problem statements, judging information, and more. Please read this carefully; most answers can be found here.
1. Your Goal: Hackathon Problem Statements

Your project must build towards one of the following problem statements:

Build for Your World - Bring Meta's models into your domain. Solve a problem you know firsthand, free up time and mental space, and make something possible that wasn't before.

Push the Frontier - Use Meta's models to tackle challenges in software, robotics, manufacturing, energy, materials and beyond. Give a machine a new capability, accelerate a scientific experiment, or unlock a better way to understand and control a physical system. Show us what becomes possible when these models meet the real world.

Your project must incorporate Meta's models. Use the Muse Spark series, Muse Wonder, Muse Image Muse Voice Transcribe and SAM 3.1 through Meta Model API, run Meta open weights models Muse Glimmer and Muse Spark Open, and code faster with Muse Code coding agent.
2. Connect with the Community

Join the Hackathon Discord to meet other participants, get official updates, begin forming teams:
Connect Discord – Meta Global AI Developer Hackathon – Cerebral Valley
Cerebral Valley

Key Channels include:

    #general: Socialize and meet other hackers.

    Open source: Repositories must be public.

    Team size: A maximum of four participants per team. Solo participants are allowed.

entries.prompt:
On Muse integration: **Partly—but the current build hasn’t yet demonstrated the most ambitious version of Soma.** We have a credible foundation. I think the next step is to give the model harder decisions within the product we already chose.

The judging language supports that interpretation: the supplied guide asks whether teams surfaced capabilities that surprised Meta. That gives us a useful target: **show a consequential decision that would be difficult to pre-script.**

I inspected the implementation. Spark currently chooses sources to read, generates grounded practice, and can repair a rejected proposal. But the quantitative lesson path mainly selects a supported configuration and parameters; several follow-up behaviors are authored rules. Browser collection currently opens selected URLs rather than letting Spark decide how to navigate.

Those are sensible foundations. They don’t yet demonstrate the full investigative and adaptive intelligence in our PRD.

**The strongest direction: Soma figures out what you need to understand, then builds an experience that tests its judgment.**

Consider this proposed demonstration:

1. **An instructor changes the assessment coverage.** The announcement refers to another document, and an older syllabus disagrees. Soma investigates the relevant sources, establishes which update applies, and changes the prepared session.
2. **Returned work reveals an ambiguous mistake.** The student might misunderstand the concept, or might understand it but have misread a diagram. Soma retains both possibilities.
3. **Soma chooses a discriminating interaction.** It prepares a question or interactive experiment whose response would help distinguish those possibilities. The activity has a specific diagnostic purpose.
4. **The student contradicts Soma’s initial interpretation.** Soma revises its hypothesis and changes the next activity instead of repeating its original explanation.
5. **The revised activity remains useful and inspectable.** The student sees what changed, the evidence behind it, and a manipulable lesson grounded in their course.

That would exercise source investigation, visual interpretation, tool use, uncertainty, and adaptation in one coherent experience. Spark’s documented multimodal inputs and multi-step tool capabilities fit that workload. Whether it performs reliably is something we need to demonstrate. [Meta’s model documentation](https://dev.meta.ai/docs/models)

The particularly interesting step is **designing the interaction**. Instead of merely asking Spark to generate another question, give it a task such as:

> “These two explanations could account for the student’s answer. Using the approved lesson model, choose an experiment that would help distinguish them.”

Spark could propose parameters, inspect the calculated result, notice that its first example doesn’t reveal the distinction, and revise it. The scientific model stays deterministic; the model decides how to use it to teach and investigate.

That gives the interactive lessons a stronger role. They become instruments Soma uses to understand and help the student, while remaining enjoyable to explore independently.

I would prioritize the work this way:

| Priority | Change | What it demonstrates |
|---|---|---|
| **First** | Let Spark choose relevant follow-up evidence when the initial source is incomplete or contradictory. | It can investigate beyond a supplied excerpt. |
| **Second** | Let Spark select a diagnostic interaction and revise its interpretation after the response. | Persistent learner context changes its decisions. |
| **Third** | Let Spark compose a meaningful experiment within the approved lesson family, using validation feedback. | The lesson reflects a reasoned instructional choice. |
| **Conditional stretch** | Model-directed, read-only browser navigation when a necessary source cannot be reached through existing collection. | It can recover and find information in a real interface. |

That last distinction matters for the submission. A browser recording only proves model computer use if the model actually chooses the actions. Meta documents that loop for both Wonder and Spark 1.3, so it is technically available; Soma still needs to implement and verify it. [Meta’s computer-use guide](https://dev.meta.ai/docs/computer-use)

**I would keep the student-facing surface small: the Ready Card, the interactive lesson, and an explanation of why the next activity changed.** The ambition belongs in the decisions behind those surfaces.

To establish that the intelligence is real, we should test variations the system hasn’t been tuned on:

- Change which source is authoritative.
- Supply evidence that overturns the apparent misconception.
- Make the first proposed experiment uninformative.
- Include an update that should leave the existing recommendation unchanged.

We should inspect the resulting actions, citations, failures, latency, and cost. If Spark consistently struggles with a specific task, that gives us a reason to compare Wonder on that task.

**My recommendation is to make “Soma investigates, designs an interaction, and changes its mind when the evidence changes” the technical ambition.** Much of that is already in our intended scope. Delivering it convincingly would strengthen the Meta story substantially while keeping the project cohesive.

# Soma learning graph scope

**Scoped October 27, 2026. Intended behavior, not implementation evidence.** This design refines PRD R5, R9, R10 and R11 and the selected returned-work hero story. The PRD owns release acceptance; the Build Plan owns dates. Existing account, source, hub, learning and evaluation requirements remain. This is a documentation handoff, not an instruction to restart the application.

## Product outcome

Soma connects course content and learning evidence, proposes explanations for a student's difficulty, and builds an interactive experiment that distinguishes those explanations. The student's response changes what the graph supports and what Soma prepares next.

The flagship is a graph that makes testable predictions and generates a useful activity from its uncertainty. Its visible payoff is an experiment tailored to a particular ambiguity in the student's work. The graph also retains the evidence needed to challenge Soma's interpretation.

## Hackathon commitment

Deliver the complete loop for one source-supported objective within the single approved quantitative family, with multiple meaningful generated configurations. The product remains multi-account and full-semester; the demonstrated scientific domain is bounded. Source fit must be confirmed before choosing the hero example. The cars/slope brainstorming example does not select another family or establish relevance to Jeremy's classes.

| Capability | Required behavior |
| --- | --- |
| Connected concepts and evidence | Stable, course-scoped concept references connect sources, lesson objectives, observations and interpretations. Show the relevant local connections and their evidence in the existing lesson inspection surface. |
| Competing explanations | Spark proposes two plausible explanations for an ambiguous response, with evidence and limitations. It may instead request clarification when two defensible explanations cannot be formed. |
| Informative experiment | Spark selects approved controls, inputs, an observable and distinct predicted responses. The numerical model checks that the proposed comparison actually distinguishes the predictions. |
| Visible predictions | The lesson presents the competing predictions and the checked result with clear labels and shared units. Hypothetical predictions never masquerade as the scientific model or as established student beliefs. |
| Student interaction | The student can predict, explore, reveal, request help or disagree. Capture prediction and reveal order; exploring without answering remains useful. |
| Graph revision | A saved response can weaken, provisionally support or leave an interpretation unresolved. Preserve the earlier version, original observation and assistance. A student correction can trigger reconsideration without rewriting course facts. |
| Changed next activity | When the new evidence warrants it, Spark prepares a materially different supported diagnostic or lesson configuration. A changed status label alone does not demonstrate adaptation. Retaining valid work or uncertainty is also a supported outcome. |
| Fresh application | Offer a different problem or representation within the supported family. Save the actual response and conditions; success cannot automatically establish another concept or course as mastered. |

The same engine serves automatic preparation, direct requests and revisits. Existing source jobs, saved responses, outbox/worker processing and publication checks carry the loop. The product must recover and resume after refresh; a manual demo trigger cannot establish automatic operation.

## The experience

1. Today has a ready activity with a source-linked reason. An applicable update or returned-work observation explains why it is here.
2. In the lesson, a compact “What Soma is checking” view presents the relevant concept, two provisional explanations and supporting observations. The student can inspect sources or correct the interpretation.
3. The interactive scene makes the disputed relationship tangible. The student can predict before revealing the checked outcome, or explore first with that assistance recorded. Displaying an explanation or answer-revealing hypothesis counts as exposure/support for the related response; the system cannot label it independent merely because the result animation was hidden.
4. A before/after explanation shows what evidence changed, which interpretation was revised and why the next activity follows. If the evidence is ambiguous, say so.
5. A fresh application checks the same relationship in a different condition. Saved history separates this observation from earlier supported work and any genuinely delayed attempt.

Use the existing Ready Card and lesson/why/evidence surfaces. The local connection view can use linked cards or a small accessible diagram; it is not a new full-screen graph destination. Every visible link should lead to evidence or an action. No force-directed semester canvas, new navigation hierarchy or arbitrary graph editor is required.

## Records and model authority

Extend the current Firestore records and investigation contracts; do not introduce a graph database or replace existing histories.

| Record | Minimum meaning |
| --- | --- |
| Concept | Stable ID, course scope, supported objective/definition, source references and versions. Similar names do not establish cross-course identity. |
| Concept relationship | Typed relationship such as prerequisite, related concept or proposed transfer; direction, scope, supporting evidence, uncertainty and supersession. Keep proposed teaching relationships distinct from learner interpretations. |
| Observation | Existing source excerpt/region, original response, correction or assistance event, with exact origin and time. |
| Interpretation | Claim, alternative explanations, linked observations, uncertainty, version and current/superseded status. Support is contextual; it is not an invented mastery percentage. |
| Diagnostic specification | Target interpretations, distinct predictions, approved model/components, inputs, observable, validation feedback and source versions. |
| Revision and next activity | Triggering observation, previous/new interpretation versions, justified activity choice, actual model/tool activity and publication state. |

Spark chooses what evidence to read, which explanations are plausible, what experiment would distinguish them and what to revise. It proposes bounded structured specifications; the application owns scientific computation, ownership, allowed relationships, source freshness, immutable observations, publishing and spending. Model-generated hypotheses cannot alter equations, validators, permissions or grading rules.

Preserve the existing call, time, repair, daily and global reservation limits. This scope does not increase the operating cap or authorize unmetered model calls. Split durable stages only through the existing bounded job and accounting rules; do not reset limits to complete a longer demonstration.

For P0, hypothetical numerical predictions use approved bounded prediction forms. Spark may select and configure those forms; it cannot install executable misconception models. Label illustrative parameters separately from numbers supplied by the course. If a relationship cannot be represented accurately, use a grounded text diagnostic and report that the interactive route is unsupported.

## What proves it works

Use the existing development and held-out evaluations; add these dimensions to their cases rather than counting reused examples as extra independent evidence.

- Before prediction reveal, two plausible explanations lead to distinguishable responses in the proposed experiment. Independently review whether they are pedagogically plausible; numerical distinguishability alone is insufficient.
- At least one contrary-response branch leads to a newly prepared supported follow-up with a different question or meaningful configuration, preserved after managed persistence/reload. Include an unchanged/ambiguous branch where forced adaptation would be wrong.
- Changing the student's response while holding the starting context fixed can change the interpretation or next action through actual Spark decisions. Do not encode the outcome in a demo scenario label.
- Source revisions invalidate affected proposals before publication. Corrections, retry, stale jobs and another account cannot overwrite or misattribute the original evidence.
- Reopening preserves records and reuses valid artifacts. A course change, response or correction triggers its authorized preparation/reconsideration path without an extra conversational instruction; queued work and completed work remain distinct.
- A fresh application has a different item/condition and truthful exposure/help records. Report transfer within the tested context, not general mastery or causal learning improvement.
- The local connection view, comparisons and controls work with keyboard, reduced motion and a readable text/numeric alternative.

Existing five-reference numerical checks, Day 3 development gate, 8/10 unseen supported generation gate, negative cases, returned-work evaluation and privacy/source gates remain unchanged. Text fallback does not count as a passed interactive flagship case.

## Stretch goals

**First stretch: one verified cross-course bridge.** With suitable sources from both courses, connect one shared relationship and offer a fresh application in the second context. Distinguish conceptual similarity from equivalence, retain each course's assumptions and test transfer rather than propagating mastery. Use the same checked family where an interactive representation is needed. Broader automatic discovery across all classes is the longer-term vision.

**Second stretch: specialized Muse evidence reasoning.** Follow [Learning Specialist Proposal](LEARNING_SPECIALIST_PROPOSAL.md): one task, one candidate open-weight model/adapter, reviewed demonstrations and an independent base-versus-tuned comparison. Its role is choosing plausible explanations and useful diagnostics. Training is conditional on a demonstrated baseline weakness, available data, verified serving path and an explicit training/serving budget. It is not necessary for the graph or flagship interaction to work, and it does not imply per-student weight updates.

**Later:** broad cross-disciplinary transfer discovery, richer learner-authored relationship editing, additional checked model families, and a semester-wide explorable graph. These remain outside the hackathon commitment.

## Delivery sequence

| Target date | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Oct 27 | Confirm the actual objective, source fit and candidate explanations; map current records/tools to this design. Register unresolved source/reviewer inputs without inventing them. |
| Oct 28 | Persist linked concepts/evidence and one complete interpretation-to-diagnostic-to-revision path. Continue existing R9 observation work and live source verification in their current dependencies. |
| Oct 29 | Checked prediction comparison and interactive variants pass the existing Day 3 lab gate. Demonstrate that an uninformative experiment is rejected or repaired. |
| Oct 30 | Complete both changed and unchanged response branches, fresh application, managed restart and accessible local inspection. Rehearse the three-minute story and capture genuine evidence. |
| Oct 31 | Feature freeze. Include a stretch only if it is implemented and checked by this point; do not add model families or training infrastructure after freeze. |
| Nov 1–4 | Existing correctness, held-out review, pilot follow-up and submission work. Assets target Nov 3; submit by Nov 4 at 9 PM America/New_York. |

The first dependency is suitable real course material and its supported scientific model, not a training job. If a date is missed, record the specific open gate and narrow release claims honestly; do not silently remove the existing scope or move the freeze.

## Three minute story

| Time | Demonstration |
| --- | --- |
| 0:00–0:35 | Ready activity and immediate manipulation: show two competing predictions and the checked relationship. |
| 0:35–1:20 | Reveal the actual work/update, supporting source and compact graph connections that motivated this experiment. Preserve required actual-source footage when supported and label its mode. |
| 1:20–2:20 | Record a student response, show genuine reconsideration and a materially changed next activity. Keep an alternate response branch available for the judge. |
| 2:20–3:00 | Show a fresh application and the existing evidence comparison with actual help and elapsed time. A cross-course bridge may occupy the fresh-application beat only if verified. |

The demonstration establishes an observed sequence of model decisions and learner actions. It makes no claim that Soma can read minds, perfectly predict a student, or infer broad mastery from one interaction.
